experiment: closed diamond-section blade and authored-face renderer parity

construction.description: Four vertices per diamond section; connect corresponding vertices with quads and explicitly cap both ends.
construction.execution: create_authored_quad_mesh through run_modeler_command_sequence; explicitly a procedural lab fixture

renderer_comparison.blender_mask: Workbench flat white, transparent background, alpha > 127
renderer_comparison.assessment: Differences are localized to a roughly two-pixel boundary band; strict pixel parity is not established. Thin silhouettes magnify IoU sensitivity. No thresholds were relaxed to claim parity.

visual_review.observed: Solid oblique render shows coherent tapered faces and a central ridge without the trident proxy's repeated compressed outlines.
limitations: Simple neutral fixture, not reference reconstruction
Ridge contrast under this studio light is weak
No SubD surface-control or cross-family transfer proof
Not evidence of autonomous repair or professional capability

next_experiment: Compare boundary errors at multiple resolutions and test ridge-preserving live subdivision against the unsubdivided cage.
